The image shows a young soybean seedling with:
- Gray/white fuzzy coating on stems
- Brown discoloration at stem node/junction area
- Small dark specks scattered on stems and leaves
- Stem appears near the soil line

Key candidates: **Charcoal_Rot** (gray stem with black microsclerotia), **Rhizoctonia** (reddish-brown sunken lesions at soil line), **Pythium_damping_off** (water-soaked soft rot).

Let me view reference images for these top candidates.
Let me also check White_Mold and Fusarium references since the test image shows white/gray fuzzy growth on stems:

**Visual observations from test image:**
- Young seedling plant near soil line
- Stem covered with gray/white fuzzy coating (possibly mycelium mixed with natural trichomes)
- Brown/gray discoloration at the stem node junction
- Small dark specks scattered on stems and leaves
- No clear water-soaked lesions; stem appears dry

**Analysis:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown, sunken, dry lesion at soil line — the node area shows brownish discoloration consistent with this
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Gray stems with scattered black microsclerotia specks — the speckled pattern on stems/leaves matches
- **Pythium**: Water-soaked soft rot on very young seedlings — the stem is not soft/water-soaked
- **White_Mold**: Fluffy white mycelium at nodes with black sclerotia — possible but typically more mature plants

The brownish-gray discoloration at the stem node with small dark specks scattered on stems is most consistent with **Rhizoctonia**, which in the reference shows a clear lesion on the young stem near soil. The Rhizoctonia reference top-right panel matches closely with the elongated gray-brown stem lesion at the soil line area.
